title: Festival FAQ
body:
# Festival FAQ

## When and where
The 32nd Annual Telluride Blues & Brews Festival runs **Friday 18 – Sunday 20 September 2026** in **Telluride Town Park**, Telluride, Colorado. Thursday 17 September carries pre-festival events in town.

## Hours
- **Gates: 11:30 AM daily.** Music in the park runs **12:00 PM – 9:30 PM**; the park closes at 9:30 PM.
- **Juke Joint shows start at 10:00 PM** in town, all within walking distance.
- **Box Office (300 E Pacific Street):** Thursday 10:00 AM – 6:30 PM · Friday & Saturday 9:00 AM – 8:15 PM · Sunday 10:00 AM – 7:15 PM.

## Rain or shine
The festival takes place rain or shine. Bring rain gear and warm clothes — September can be chilly in Telluride.

## Seating and tarps
General admission. **Tarps do not reserve exclusive seating** — if a tarp is unattended, other people may sit there until the owner returns. No high-back chairs between the sound booth and the stage.

*Note for staff: the packing list caps tarps at 5' × 8' while the line policy says one number equals one 10' × 10' tarp. Those two published rules conflict on the official site and need reconciling.*

## The entry line
- **No line formation before 5:00 PM Thursday.**
- You must be physically in line — no empty chairs holding a place; unattended chairs are removed.
- **Numbers are handed out each morning before gates open.** Once you have a number you need to stay in line, though bathroom and coffee breaks are fine.
- **No camping in line** — no tents, no sleeping, no cooking. That is town ordinance, not a festival rule.
- **One number = one person = one 10' × 10' tarp.**
- Entry proceeds in number order after security screening.

## Kids
Children **11 and under are free** and must be accompanied by an adult. See the Kids Area page.

## Pets
**No pets** on the festival grounds or in the campground. This is Town Park law and is strictly enforced. Do not leave a pet in a car or tied to one. Service animals are permitted in the campground with documentation.

Boarding options listed by the festival:
- Montrose Veterinary Clinic — 970-249-5469
- Deleff Kennels, Delta — 970-874-4058
- Cottonwood Ranch & Kennel, Crawford — 970-921-7100
- Wag Resort, Grand Junction — 970-241-2949
- Iron Will Dog Lodge, Montrose — 970-596-8709

## On the grounds
Free drinking water (bring your own bottle) · plenty of port-a-potties · hand sinks · trash, recycling and compost stations · food and craft vendors · beer, wine and cocktails for purchase · the Rainbow Kids Area · a **Medical Tent on the east edge of the grounds**, campground side, where EMTs carry basics like ibuprofen and sunblock.

**Lost & Found** is at the warming hut next to the Town Park Oval, on the path from the Box Office to the main entrance.

## Leaving with a drink
You **may not** leave the festival grounds carrying a glass of beer or wine. That is a local ordinance and it is strictly enforced.

## Fire restrictions
As of 1 September 2026 the **Telluride Fire Protection District is in Stage 2 fire restrictions**. Check the San Miguel Sheriff's Office and West Slope Fire Information for current status — this changes quickly.

## Contact
Telluride Blues & Brews Festival, 500 East Colorado Avenue, Telluride, CO 81435
Phone **(970) 728-8037** · Email **Grant@sbgproductions.com**

*Note for staff: the site footer prints the ZIP as 81320. Telluride's ZIP is 81435. This looks like a long-standing typo.*

## Not answered by the festival
The official FAQ does not address **re-entry** policy. If you need to leave and come back, ask at the gate.

*Note for staff: the Juke Joints price is printed as $35 on the tickets page and $30 on the late-night-shows page. The $35 figure is used here.*

## What each pass covers
- **GA 3-Day** — Main Stage and Blues Stage.
- **Single-Day** — Main Stage, Blues Stage and Truck Stage.
- **VIP** — exclusive lounges, viewing platform, raw bar, early Juke Joint entry, VIP reception, gospel brunch, premium restrooms.
- **Super VIP** — everything in VIP plus an on-stage lounge, sky deck viewing, chef station, open bar, backstage access, golf cart shuttle and personal concierges.

## Beer tasting sessions
Tasting session tickets are **separate** from festival entry. You must be **21+** *and* hold a Single-Day or 3-Day festival pass to enter a session.

## Refunds and exchanges
**All sales are final. Tickets are non-refundable and non-exchangeable.** The one exception: sold-out ticket types can be listed for exchange through the official exchange.

title: Wristbands — 2026 Policy Change
body:
# Wristbands — what changed for 2026

## Wristbands are not being mailed
**In 2026, wristbands will NOT be mailed.** All admission wristbands are distributed **on-site during festival week**. If you are used to a package arriving in the post, it is not coming this year.

## How to get yours
1. About **one week before the festival**, Front Gate emails you a **digital ticket**.
2. Bring that digital ticket — printed or on your phone — **plus valid photo ID** to the **Box Office at 300 E Pacific Street**.
3. **Each ticket-holder must be present in person.** You cannot pick up a wristband for someone else, even a partner or a family member travelling with you.

**Box Office hours:** Thursday 10:00 AM – 6:30 PM · Friday & Saturday 9:00 AM – 8:15 PM · Sunday 10:00 AM – 7:15 PM.

## Wearing it
- It must be worn **snugly** and must not be able to slip on and off.
- **Do not remove it between days.**
- Tampering with a wristband, stretching it, or wearing it loose means **confiscation with no replacement**.
- **Only Front Gate wristbands are valid.** Counterfeits are seized on sight.

## Taking it off afterwards
Cut it at the end where the cloth strap is sewn to the clasp.

title: Gondola, Shuttles & Parking
body:
# Getting around

Telluride is a small town at the end of a box canyon. Almost everything festival-related is walkable, and what isn't is covered by free transit.

## The gondola — free
The Telluride–Mountain Village gondola is **free**. Festival-week hours:

| Day | Hours |
|---|---|
| Thursday | 6:30 AM – 12:00 AM |
| Friday & Saturday | 6:30 AM – 2:00 AM |
| Sunday | 6:30 AM – 12:00 AM |

Stations, west to east: **Telluride Station (Oak Street)** → **Station San Sophia** (mid-mountain ridge; Allred's, The Ridge Club, ski trails) → **Mountain Village Station** (village core), with a short additional stretch to **Market Plaza Station** (parking garage, Town Hall, Mountain Market). The ride takes about **12 minutes** and the system runs on wind power purchased from San Miguel Power Association.

*Station names, ride time and the wind-power detail come from Visit Telluride and TMVOA, not from the festival site.*

Telluride Station is at the **west end of town** — the opposite end from Town Park.

## Free shuttles
- **Galloping Goose (Telluride)** — fixed laps every **20 minutes**, **7:00 AM – midnight** during the concert weekend. Stops every few blocks, marked by signs.
- **Mountain Village shuttles** — every **30 minutes**.
- **Mountain Village Dial-A-Ride** — daily **7:00 AM – 12:30 AM**, **(970) 728-8888**.

## Ground transport
**Telluride Express** is the official ground-transport partner, serving Telluride and the Montrose, Grand Junction, Durango, Cortez and Gunnison airports with door-to-door shared, private and custom rides. **(970) 728-6000**.

## Airports
**Telluride Regional Airport** sits at **9,070 feet** — described as North America's highest commercial airport — about **15 minutes** from Telluride or Mountain Village. Also served by Montrose, Durango, Cortez and Grand Junction, with international connections through Denver, Salt Lake City and Albuquerque.

Road conditions: **(877) 315-7623**.

## Parking
**There is no festival parking lot.** Park in any legal spot in Telluride or Mountain Village. If Telluride is full you may be directed to Mountain Village — take the gondola in.

- **Main Street and side streets** are metered, enforced **8:00 AM – 6:00 PM Monday–Saturday**, **$0.50/hour**, three-hour maximum. **Not enforced on Sundays.**
- During the festival weekend the **O, G and W residential permit zones do not apply** — you may leave a vehicle there for the duration.
- **SilverJack Parking Garage, 155 W Pacific Avenue** — $2.00/hour plus a **$50/night** overnight fee.
- **Gondola Parking Garage (Mountain Village)** — free 6:30 AM – 2:00 AM, **$30 overnight**. The most convenient Mountain Village option.
- **No parking on South Oak Street Friday 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM** — Telluride Farmers' Market.
- **Car camping is prohibited** in public lots, on streets, and in public rights-of-way in Telluride, Mountain Village and Lawson Hill.

## Information Station
Camping, parking and ticket questions are answered at the **Information Station at the entrance to town**, open **9:00 AM – 5:00 PM Thursday through Saturday**.

title: Camping
body:
# Camping

All three camping areas are roughly a **2–3 minute walk from the festival entrance**. Camping is **communal — there are no designated or reserved campsites**. First come, first served.

## Warner Field — 4-Day Camping, $70
Open **Thursday through Monday**. At the **baseball field entrance to Town Park**. Treeless and open, directly adjacent to the Beer Garden and the Tasting Sessions.
**Propane grills and BBQs are allowed. Charcoal is prohibited here.**

## Main Campground — 5-Day Camping, $80
Open **Wednesday through Monday**. A large wooded area **east of the festival grounds**, backing onto Bear Creek Wilderness. This is where the **Campground Stage** sits among the trees by the river.
**Charcoal and propane are both permitted.**

## Zone 1 — 5-Day Camping, $80
Open **Wednesday through Monday**. A smaller wooded section in the **southeast corner of the Main Campground**, adjacent to Bear Creek Wilderness.
**Charcoal and propane are both permitted.**

## Amenities
- Flushing toilets
- **Token-operated showers — $1 per roughly 75 seconds**
- Limited electrical charging stations
- Lost & Found at the warming hut

## Rules
- **No pets.** Service animals with documentation are the only exception.
- **No camping within 50 feet of Bear Creek Falls.**
- **No wood fires.** Charcoal only, in designated containers, and only where charcoal is permitted.
- **No vehicles entering or exiting during the festival.**
- **All campers must vacate by 11:00 AM Monday.**

## Arriving
Campers get a **30-minute grace period** to drive in and drop gear. Volunteers direct you and arrange wagons, then staff guide you out to off-site parking.

## Fire restrictions
As of 1 September 2026 the **Telluride Fire Protection District is in Stage 2 fire restrictions**. This can change your cooking options at short notice — check before you travel.

title: What to Bring / What Not to Bring
body:
# What to bring

- **Valid photo ID** — required to collect your wristband, and for anything 21+
- Sunscreen and a hat
- **Lawn chairs** — but **no high-back chairs between the sound booth and the stage**
- **Tarps and blankets — no bigger than 5' × 8'.** Share the space when you are not using it
- **Sunshade tents — back perimeter only**, in "Shade Alley"
- **Coolers** with **unopened** plastic water and soda bottles, cans, and unopened food. Coolers are searched at the gate
- A camera — **non-professional only**
- Strollers
- **Warm clothes.** September can be chilly in Telluride
- **Rain gear.** The festival takes place rain or shine
- An empty bottle for the free drinking water on the grounds

*Note for staff: the packing list caps tarps at 5' × 8' while the entry-line policy says one number equals one 10' × 10' tarp. Those two published rules conflict.*

# What NOT to bring

- **No glass** anywhere on the grounds
- **No pets** on the grounds or in the campground — strictly enforced
- **No outside alcohol**
- **No illegal drugs**
- **No unlicensed vending**
- **No professional photo equipment, video cameras or video recording gear**
- **No frisbees**
- **No shelled nuts**
- **No weapons**

And one that catches people out: **you may not leave the festival carrying a glass of beer or wine.** That is a local ordinance and it is strictly enforced.

title: Altitude & Weather
body:
# Altitude & weather

## How high you are
**Telluride sits at 8,750 feet** in the San Juan Mountains — that is the festival's own figure. (Wikipedia gives the town elevation as 8,754 ft / 2,668 m.) **Telluride Regional Airport is at 9,070 feet**, described as North America's highest commercial airport, about 15 minutes away.

If you have flown in from sea level, you are a long way up and you will feel it.

## Altitude advice — from this app, not from the festival
**The festival does not publish altitude guidance.** Everything in this section is app-authored general advice and is not festival policy:

- Drink far more water than feels necessary, starting the day before you arrive. Free drinking water is available on the grounds — bring a bottle.
- Go easy on alcohol on day one. Drinks hit noticeably harder at 8,750 feet, and the festival is a beer festival.
- Give yourself a day to arrive before doing anything strenuous if you can.
- Headache, breathlessness, poor sleep and loss of appetite are the common early signs of altitude affecting you. If symptoms get worse rather than better, go to the **Medical Tent on the east edge of the grounds**.

## Weather
**The festival takes place rain or shine.**

The festival's own packing list calls for **warm clothes** — "September can be chilly in Telluride" — and **rain gear**. Take both seriously: the temperature swing between a sunny afternoon and a 9:30 PM headline set at this elevation is large.

*App-authored note, not published by the festival: late-summer afternoons in the San Juan Mountains often bring short, sharp thunderstorms. A packable rain layer is worth more than an umbrella in a crowd.*

## Fire restrictions
As of 1 September 2026 the **Telluride Fire Protection District is in Stage 2 fire restrictions**. The festival points to the San Miguel Sheriff's Office and West Slope Fire Information for current detail. This is volatile — check close to your travel date.

title: Accessibility
body:
# Accessibility

## What the festival provides
- **The festival is wheelchair accessible.**
- There is a **designated space for wheelchair users directly in front of the sound booth**, which is out in the crowd facing the Main Stage.
- **Handicap restrooms and porta-potties** are on the grounds.
- **Limited handicap parking** is available in the Telluride Town Park parking lot, reached **over the vehicle bridge at the main entrance to the Park**.
- **Service animals are permitted in the campground with documentation.** Pets are not, under any circumstances.

## Seating rules that affect sightlines
**High-back chairs are not permitted between the sound booth and the stage.** The sound booth marks the boundary of the front-of-house zone.

## Getting to the grounds
The free **Galloping Goose** shuttle runs fixed laps every 20 minutes from 7:00 AM to midnight during the concert weekend, and **Mountain Village Dial-A-Ride** ((970) 728-8888) operates 7:00 AM – 12:30 AM daily.

## What is not published
The festival does **not** publish information on **ASL interpretation, sensory accommodations, or an accessibility hotline**. If you need any of those, contact the festival directly before you travel:

**(970) 728-8037** · **Grant@sbgproductions.com**

title: Kids at the Festival
body:
# Kids at the festival

## Admission
**Children 11 and under get in free** and must be accompanied by an adult.

## Rainbow Kids Area
In the **back northeast section of the festival grounds**. For **ages 3 and up**.

What's there:
- A climbing wall
- Inflatable bounce games
- Face painting
- A talent show
- Children's workshops
- **Parades on Saturday and Sunday**
- Entertainment from the **Living Folklore Clowns** — "Giggly Sprout" and "Gumbo Wobbly"

## Costs
**Fees are charged for the games**, payable at the Kids Area itself.

**The festival does not publish the game prices or the Kids Area opening hours.** Ask at the Kids Area or the Information Station when you arrive — this app cannot tell you, because the numbers are not published.

## Practical notes for families
- **Strollers are allowed.**
- Free drinking water is available on the grounds — bring a bottle.
- The **Medical Tent** is on the east edge of the grounds, campground side.
- **No shelled nuts** are permitted on the grounds.
- **Lost & Found** is at the warming hut next to the Town Park Oval, on the path from the Box Office to the main entrance.
- Music in the park runs until 9:30 PM. Nights get cold at 8,750 feet — bring layers for children as well as yourselves.
